title.suggested: Allen covers Goss's stake for coming match

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Evening Dispatch reported that Allen had covered Joe Goss's $500 stake and that the men would meet in Cincinnati on the 12th to set the purse, from $1,000 a side up.

metadata.notes: 1876-05-02 is before 1878-12. Headline: "The Coming Match Between Tom Allen and Joe Goss."

facts.fact: Joe Goss put up $500 in Cincinnati and Allen covered it; the two sides were to meet at Cincinnati on May 12 to agree the purse, open from $1,000 a side
Allen said he would fight Goss for any amount within twelve weeks, to be fought in the Southwest; he weighed 195 pounds and could reduce to 178
Allen said he had been badly treated by parties in St. Louis while he was in Chicago and expressed contempt for Coburn and his gang

notes: See 077 for the same match in the Republican.
